summary_en: This Phase 1 study is testing FX-111, a drug taken by mouth, in adult men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Participants take FX-111 once daily in continuous 28-day cycles; the total duration is not stated. The study measures side effects (safety and tolerability) and whether FX-111 reduces or prevents cancer progression.
summary_es: Este estudio de Fase 1 evalúa FX-111, un medicamento que se toma por vía oral, en hombres adultos con cáncer de próstata metastásico resistente a la castración. Los participantes toman FX-111 una vez al día en ciclos continuos de 28 días; la duración total no se indica. El estudio mide los efectos secundarios (seguridad y tolerabilidad) y si FX-111 reduce o previene la progresión del cáncer.
who_for: Adult men with confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma.
PSA at least 2 ng/mL at screening, with two consecutive rises at least 1 week apart.
Cancer progressed on hormone therapy and at least one prior potent AR pathway inhibitor.
Continuing hormone therapy with a GnRH agonist or antagonist, unless both testicles were removed.
Agrees to highly effective contraception during the study and for 90 days after.
not_for: Predominant small cell or neuroendocrine prostate cancer on the most recent biopsy.
Brain metastases needing ongoing radiation or high-dose steroids.
Prior treatment with AR degraders or AR ligand molecules such as RIPTAC.
Blood clots within 4 weeks before starting treatment.
Concurrent malignancy needing treatment, or a prior malignancy active within 2 years (unless clinically stable or treated with curative intent).
